sources.entry: Thanos | Highly available Prometheus setup with long term storage capabilities

summary.one_liner: Thanos is a set of components that extends existing Prometheus deployments with a global query view, high availability, and unlimited long-term metric storage in object storage.
summary.what_it_does: Thanos composes multiple components into a highly available metrics system that sits on top of existing Prometheus installations. It provides a global query view across all connected Prometheus servers and can deduplicate and merge data from Prometheus HA pairs. Historical metrics are stored in any object storage using the Prometheus 2.0 storage format, with optional downsampling to speed up queries over old data. The README also mentions cross-cluster federation, fault-tolerant query routing, and a gRPC "Store API" for unified access to metric data. The README describes a Sidecar deployment for Kubernetes and a Receive component for scaling out or working with other remote-write compatible sources.
use_cases: Querying metrics across multiple Prometheus servers or clusters
Deduplicating metrics from Prometheus HA pairs
Storing historical metrics in object storage
stack: Docker images (quay.io/thanos/thanos, thanosio/thanos on Docker Hub)
notable: Runs alongside existing Prometheus deployments without replacing them
Object storage is the only optional external dependency
Global query view across all connected Prometheus servers
Downsampling of historical data for faster queries
Minor releases roughly every 6 weeks with tarballs and Docker images
caveats: The README does not include install or run instructions; it links to external docs for setup
Described as a CNCF Incubating project; the README does not state platform limits or costs
